lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 104, which makes CI's code review wait for its checking agents before it reports.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one oh four, which makes CI's code review wait for its checking agents before it reports.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The prompt now says to start all checking agents at once, wait for each, and mark each answer checked.
First, the reviewer runs the code-review skill on the pushed diff, as before.
Then it checks each new finding with its own agent, started together with the next step's agents.
The agents re-checking findings still open from earlier reviews run at the same time, and it waits for all of them.
It returns its output only after every agent has reported, with each answer marked checked.
The collect step then fails the job if any open finding got no answer.
It also fails it when an answer isn't marked checked, or says an agent hadn't reported.
The comment then says why, nothing is recorded as not fixed, and re-running the review job retries.
On PR #102 the reviewer answered before its agents reported, so that PR needed six review rounds.
lines.say: On pull request one oh two the reviewer answered before its agents reported, so that pull request needed six review rounds.

lines.caption: It wasn't a timeout. The agents ran in the background, and nothing told the reviewer to wait.
Step 2 starts both batches of agents in one message, with background off, and waits for every one before the fix.
Step 4 returns an answer for every open finding, each with a checked flag that is true only if its agent reported.
Steps 5 and 6 are the script's checks: every open id answered, and every new finding and answer checked.
The findings and fix are still saved, and the code review comment names the reason and asks for a re-run.
Here are the checks: one for missing answers, one for unchecked findings and answers, and the saved reason.
The checked flag is the main check. The wording is a backup that needs a timing word or a sentence end.
The review script changes, one line of the workflow uploads the reason, plus this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert the one commit.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The checks were tried with fake review output after all fixes. A real review at #102's head was not run.
lines.say: The checks were tried with fake review output after all fixes. A real review at one oh two's head was not run.

lines.caption: The wording comes from #102's own reviews, where the agents never reported.
lines.say: The wording comes from one oh two's own reviews, where the agents never reported.

lines.caption: The prompt already ran agents in parallel. The PR starts both batches together and adds the wait.
After all fixes, a dry run with an open finding left unanswered failed and named it.
The two not-reported sentences from #102 both failed the dry run.
lines.say: The two not-reported sentences from one oh two both failed the dry run.

lines.caption: Two ordinary notes passed. A review with nothing open passed too, but only before the first fix round.
An unchecked finding failed, and a run with both problems named both, in dry runs before the latest fixes.
After the latest fixes, a new finding left unchecked failed, and so did four bare not-reported notes.
A lower-case id still matched, and a stray old id was ignored.
A previous entry with no id no longer stops the collect step.
Re-running the review at #102's head was not run. That PR belongs to another session.
lines.say: Re-running the review at one oh two's head was not run. That pull request belongs to another session.

lines.caption: A fresh agent found one problem, fixed. Two later ones found three low notes each, and five were fixed.
The first wording check also matched ordinary sentences. It is stricter now.
It checked the rest and found it fine.
The second review's notes widened the backup wording and limited the checked rule to the findings that matter.
The third review's gaps added yet and more sentence ends; one unlikely false match was left.
CI's first review found R1 to R9. R1, a confirmed medium, failed the review job.
Now a failed collect keeps its findings and fix, and the comment says why it failed.
Answers carry the checked flag, and ids match whatever their case or spacing.
Both batches of agents now start together, so the fix has every verdict.
R9 was disproved by the review itself, so nothing changed for it.
CI's second review passed. R1, R2 and R4 were resolved, and R5 to R9 are unconfirmed.
lines.say: C I's second review passed. R one, R two and R four were resolved, and R five to R nine are unconfirmed.

lines.caption: R3 is still open: a failed collect drops the run's findings, as the issue asks. It waits on your decision.
lines.say: R three is still open: a failed collect drops the run's findings, as the issue asks. It waits on your decision.

lines.caption: R10 to R12 were fixed: every new finding is checked, bare notes are caught, and odd ids are skipped.
lines.say: R ten to R twelve were fixed: every new finding is checked, bare notes are caught, and odd ids are skipped.

lines.caption: R13 to R16 are accepted: each is asked for, harmless, or kept on purpose.
lines.say: R thirteen to R sixteen are accepted: each is asked for, harmless, or kept on purpose.

lines.caption: They are low, unconfirmed and from a later review, so a trailer on this explainer commit accepts them.
The push with the R10 to R12 fixes gets its own CI review, linked through the code review comment.
lines.say: The push with the R ten to R twelve fixes gets its own C I review, linked through the code review comment.

lines.caption: Only real reviews after the merge show an open finding, fixed in another file, coming back resolved.
They also show how much longer reviews get against the 30-minute limit.
lines.say: They also show how much longer reviews get against the thirty-minute limit.

lines.caption: The links lead to the PR and to the issue with #102's evidence.
lines.say: The links lead to the pull request and to the issue with one oh two's evidence.

lines.caption: Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue builds on this one. The next reviews are the test.
Every finding gets checked before the report, so you should see fewer review rounds.
In short: the review now waits for its agents, or fails and is re-run.
